title: Quiz: Area of Triangle using Sine

questions.stem: The formula for the area of a triangle using sine is:
questions.explanation: The area of a triangle is $\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$, where $a$ and $b$ are two sides and $C$ is the included angle.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides $8$ cm and $11$ cm with an included angle of $40°$. What is its area to $1$ decimal place?
The angle used in the sine area formula must be:

options.text: The included angle between the two known sides

questions.explanation: The angle must be the included angle between the two sides being used in the formula.

questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has side $6$ cm. What is its exact area?
A triangle has an area of $24$ cm$^2$. Two sides are $8$ cm and $10$ cm. What is the included angle to $1$ decimal place?
A parallelogram has sides $6$ cm and $10$ cm with an angle of $70°$ between them. What is its area to $1$ decimal place?
questions.explanation: A parallelogram can be split into two triangles, so area $= 6 \times 10 \times \sin 70° = 60 \times 0.9397 = 56.4$ cm$^2$.

questions.stem: The maximum area of a triangle with two sides of $5$ cm and $8$ cm occurs when the included angle is:
questions.explanation: Area $= \frac{1}{2}(5)(8)\sin C$. Since $\sin C$ is maximised when $C = 90°$ (where $\sin 90° = 1$), the maximum area is $20$ cm$^2$.
